newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Election jitters hits Paris bourse, rest mixed.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Election jitters hits Paris bourse, rest mixed.

text.p: Pre-election jitters in France drove the Paris bourse down steeply on Tuesday while the rest of Europe put in a mixed performance in thin trading.

In currencies, the dollar climbed against the yen but made only little headway against the mark. The German currency has been bolstered by the announcement of the French election, which casts a cloud over progress towards European monetary union.
The fall in Paris stocks was a big surprise after the political uncertainty was cleared away by President Jacques Chirac who last night called snap elections for May-June.
After heavy losses on Monday, French shares rebounded strongly at the start following Chirac's announcement--only to tumble by one percent on the blue chip CAC-40 index at one point.

Chirac said the early poll was needed to prepare France for a single European currency and give his centre-right coalition a five-year mandate to reform the state, reduce public spending and cut taxes and welfare charges.
Socialist leader Lionel Jospin said the Socialists too favour the single currency -- but not at the price of an extra bout of austerity.
"There's a chance the Socialists could come to power and that scares people," a trader said.
The trader said the government's decision to delay the partial privatisation of France Telecom by a month because of the election also depressed the bourse.
Even if Chirac's conservative RPR party returns with a majority, expectations that the government will push through austerity measures disheartened equities investors.
"If they raise taxes, that will hurt consumption more, and if they cut taxes, it could lead to social unrest because in France it would be viewed as 'the rich getting richer'," a trader said.

"We'll be eating, drinking and sleeping polls over the next few weeks," a bond analyst at a French bank said. Traders said the mood was nervous and few investors were willing to stick their necks out by buying until the political horizon became clearer.

London, Europe's biggest bourse, was among the best performers, climbing 0.25 percent on the FTSE index despite worries about the May 1 British election and a possible interest rate rise shortly after.
A strong showing in the banking, pharmaceutical and oil sectors pushed the anxieties into the background but trading was thin.
"The market is higher but the gains aren't broad-based. I can't see the FTSE going that much higher today," the head of trading at a large brokerage said.
The market managed to shake off early losses which came on the heels of a weaker performance in New York overnight. Wall Street opened higher on Tuesday.
In Frankfurt, stocks traded on the floor ended the session slightly down after investors took profits but the computerised IBIS index was still up by midafternoon.
Traders also said it appeared that the German market was benefiting from the uncertain French political outlook, with some investors apparently shifting funds out of French stocks into the DAX.
On the currency front, dollar crept higher against the yen but kept within a narrow range. The mood was cautious ahead of the weekend meeting of G7 industrialised countries and the French election.
Against the mark, the dollar made only slight progress because the German currency was helped by the new element of uncertainty over the single currency brought by the French election.
Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said late Monday that an EMU delay could be considered if big countries were to miss the convergence criteria.
The U.S. currency was also given a lift by a bullish dollar outlook in Germany's leading economic institutes' spring report.
CURRENCIES AT 1400GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7093 marks and 126.18 yen after ending at 1.7035 and 125.63 in late trading in Europe on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1400 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 13.5 points at 4,342.2.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 16.49 points at 2,506.08.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended down 7.25 points at 3,340.33.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $341.60 an ounce, compared to Monday's close of $342.25. Silver was three cents up at $4.77.
